dataset: Sampled heliocentric trajectories for four spacecraft, and surface coordinates for two Mars rover sites
sample_format: each sample is [jd, x, y, z]: Julian day (TDB) and position in au
numbers_note: Trajectory samples and rover coordinates are stored as JSON numbers, not strings, because of bulk; each parsed number round-trips to the digits served by its source.

voyager1.sampling: 4 day step from 1977-09-05 14:00 TDB to 1981-01-01, then 30 day step to 2026-08-16, plus a final point at JD 2461268.5 (2026-08-16 00:00 TDB)
voyager1.coverage_note: The Horizons API reports no ephemeris for Voyager 1 prior to A.D. 1977-Sep-05 13:59:24.3830 TDB; a vectors request through 2050-01-01 succeeds, so coverage extends at least that far. Sampling here stops at 2026-08-16. The later samples are the projected trajectory Horizons serves through 2050-01-01.
voyager1.source: https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api with EPHEM_TYPE=VECTORS, CENTER='500@10', REF_PLANE=ECLIPTIC, OUT_UNITS=AU-D, CSV_FORMAT=YES, VEC_TABLE=1, COMMAND='-31'
voyager1.mission_note: Launched 5 September 1977; entered interstellar space in August 2012; still operating, with two science instruments returning data.

voyager2.sampling: 8 day step from 1977-08-20 16:00 TDB to 1990-01-01, then 30 day step to 2026-08-16, plus a final point at JD 2461268.5 (2026-08-16 00:00 TDB)
voyager2.coverage_note: The Horizons API reports no ephemeris for Voyager 2 prior to A.D. 1977-Aug-20 15:32:32.1830 TDB; a vectors request through 2050-01-01 succeeds, so coverage extends at least that far. Sampling here stops at 2026-08-16. The later samples are the projected trajectory Horizons serves through 2050-01-01.
voyager2.source: https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api with EPHEM_TYPE=VECTORS, CENTER='500@10', REF_PLANE=ECLIPTIC, OUT_UNITS=AU-D, CSV_FORMAT=YES, VEC_TABLE=1, COMMAND='-32'
voyager2.mission_note: Launched 20 August 1977; flew past Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, the only spacecraft to have studied all four giant planets at close range; entered interstellar space on 10 December 2018; the extended mission continues.

cassini.sampling: 5 day step from 1997-10-15 10:00 TDB to 2004-07-01 (interplanetary cruise), then 10 day step to 2017-09-15 (Saturn orbit), plus a final point at JD 2458011.99792 (2017-09-15 11:57:00 TDB)
cassini.coverage_note: The Horizons API reports no ephemeris for Cassini prior to A.D. 1997-Oct-15 09:27:11.5724 TDB and none after A.D. 2017-Sep-15 11:58:00.0000 TDB, the atmospheric entry at Saturn that ended the mission.
cassini.source: https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api with EPHEM_TYPE=VECTORS, CENTER='500@10', REF_PLANE=ECLIPTIC, OUT_UNITS=AU-D, CSV_FORMAT=YES, VEC_TABLE=1, COMMAND='-82'
cassini.mission_note: Launched 15 October 1997; studied Saturn, its rings and its moons from orbit beginning in 2004; the mission ended on 15 September 2017 with a deliberate plunge into Saturn's atmosphere.

new_horizons.sampling: 6 day step from 2006-01-19 20:00 TDB to 2026-08-16, plus a final point at JD 2461268.5 (2026-08-16 00:00 TDB)
new_horizons.coverage_note: The Horizons API reports no ephemeris for New Horizons prior to A.D. 2006-Jan-19 19:51:18.3305 TDB; a vectors request through 2050-01-01 succeeds, so coverage extends at least that far. Sampling here stops at 2026-08-16. The later samples are the projected trajectory Horizons serves through 2050-01-01.
new_horizons.source: https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api with EPHEM_TYPE=VECTORS, CENTER='500@10', REF_PLANE=ECLIPTIC, OUT_UNITS=AU-D, CSV_FORMAT=YES, VEC_TABLE=1, COMMAND='-98'
new_horizons.mission_note: Launched 19 January 2006; flew past Pluto on 14 July 2015 and Arrokoth on 1 January 2019; continues outward from the Sun gathering heliophysics data.

perseverance.rover_position_note: End-of-drive localisation for the latest drive published in the mission waypoint feed; latitude positive north, longitude positive east, as served.
perseverance.latitude_convention_note: The waypoint feed and the Mars24 page publish latitude and longitude without stating whether the latitude is areocentric or areographic, so that attribute is null for the rover coordinates. The USGS Gazetteer crater entries state their coordinate system explicitly: planetocentric (areocentric), +East.
perseverance.landing_note: Landed 18 February 2021 in Jezero Crater, at 77.45 degrees east, 18.44 degrees north, as printed by the cited NASA page.
perseverance.crater_center_note: Centre of Jezero crater from the USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, coordinate system stated as planetocentric, +East.
perseverance.mission_note: Mars 2020 rover; landed in Jezero crater on 18 February 2021 and continues to operate there.

curiosity.rover_position_note: Final waypoint of the latest drive published in the mission waypoint feed; latitude positive north, longitude positive east, as served.
curiosity.latitude_convention_note: The waypoint feed and the Mars24 page publish latitude and longitude without stating whether the latitude is areocentric or areographic, so that attribute is null for the rover coordinates. The USGS Gazetteer crater entries state their coordinate system explicitly: planetocentric (areocentric), +East.
curiosity.landing_note: Landed 6 August 2012 (UTC) in Gale Crater, at 137.44 degrees east, 4.59 degrees south, as printed by the cited NASA page; the stored latitude applies the sign convention south negative.
curiosity.crater_center_note: Centre of Gale crater from the USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, coordinate system stated as planetocentric, +East.
curiosity.mission_note: Mars Science Laboratory rover; landed in Gale Crater on 6 August 2012 and continues to operate there.
